description: Leaving a job, founding a company or taking a pay cut for a better trajectory all require slack. A permit tied to an employer removes the option entirely; an open application makes any change look like a risk to the file.
energy_note: Every career move is also an immigration decision.

aspect: You cannot negotiate from a visa
description: An employee whose status depends on the employer has materially less bargaining power, and both sides know it. The salary gap compounds across every subsequent offer, which are benchmarked against it.
money_note: Cumulative differential over a career - illustrative.

aspect: SCENARIO - the raise he did not ask for
description: Omid has been underpaid by roughly CAD 18,000 for two years. He knows. His PR application names this employer. He decides to ask after it lands, which is what he decided last year.
energy_note: Every year the right time to ask is next year.

aspect: SCENARIO - the company he did not found
description: Two colleagues leave to start something and ask Omid to join as the third. Founding requires giving up the employer-tied permit. He says no and stays. The company is acquired four years later.
energy_note: The fork in the road, foreclosed by paperwork.

aspect: And it is read as a personality
description: From outside, all of this looks like caution, or lack of ambition, or not being a self-starter. It is a rational response to conditions nobody in the room can see.
energy_note: Your constraints, mistaken for your character.
